subtopics.content: The aim of the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) syllabus in Chemistry is to prepare candidates for the Board's examination.
subtopics.objective: Understand the basic principles and concepts in chemistry; interpret scientific data relating to chemistry; deduce relationships between chemistry and other sciences; apply chemistry knowledge to industry and everyday life.

topics.title: Separation of Mixtures and Purification of Chemical Substances

subtopics.content: Elements, compounds and mixtures; chemical and physical changes; pure and impure substances; boiling, density, freezing and melting points; separation processes including evaporation, simple and fractional distillation, sublimation, recrystallization, paper and column chromatography, simple and fractional crystallization, magnetization, decantation, filtration and centrifugation.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between elements, compounds and mixtures; differentiate between chemical and physical changes; distinguish between pure and impure substances; use boiling and melting points as criteria for purity; identify the properties of mixture components; specify the principles involved in separation methods; apply separation principles in everyday life.

subtopics.content: Laws of definite, multiple and reciprocal proportions; law of conservation of matter; chemical symbols, formulae and equations and their uses; relative atomic mass based on 12C = 12; mole concept and stoichiometry of reactions.
subtopics.objective: Deduce chemical laws from given expressions, statements or data; perform simple calculations involving formulae, equations, chemical composition and the mole concept; deduce the stoichiometry of chemical reactions.

topics.title: Kinetic Theory of Matter and Gas Laws

subtopics.content: Phenomena supporting the kinetic theory of matter: melting, vaporization, boiling, freezing and condensation, explained in terms of molecular motion and Brownian movement. Boyle's, Charles's, Avogadro's, Gay-Lussac's, Graham's and Dalton's laws of partial pressure; molar volume and atomicity of gases; ideal gas equation PV = nRT; relationship between vapour density and relative molecular mass; ideal and real gases.
subtopics.objective: Apply the theory to distinguish solids, liquids and gases; deduce reasons for changes of state; draw inferences based on molecular motion; deduce gas laws from expressions, statements or data; interpret graphs related to gas laws; perform simple calculations using gas laws, equations and relationships; state factors responsible for deviations of real gases from ideal behaviour.

subtopics.content: Concepts of atoms, molecules and ions; contributions of Dalton, Millikan, Rutherford, Moseley, Thomson and Bohr to atomic theory; atomic structure, four quantum numbers, principles governing electron arrangement in orbitals, electron configuration, atomic number, mass number and isotopes, with examples from elements of atomic numbers 1–20; shapes of s and p orbitals.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between atoms, molecules and ions; identify the contributions of scientists to atomic theory; deduce the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons from atomic and mass numbers; apply rules governing electron arrangement; identify common isotopic elements; relate isotopy to mass number; perform simple isotope calculations; differentiate orbital shapes; determine the number of electrons in s and p atomic orbitals.

subtopics.content: The periodic table and periodicity of elements; recognition of families such as alkali metals, alkaline-earth metals, halogens, noble gases and transition metals; variation in ionization energy, ionic radii, electron affinity, electronegativity, electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity.
subtopics.objective: Relate atomic number to an element's position in the periodic table; relate properties of elements to their groups; explain variations in properties across periods and down groups.

subtopics.content: Chemical bonding: electrovalency and covalency; electron configurations and tendency to attain noble-gas structures; hydrogen bonding and metallic bonding; coordinate covalent bonds illustrated by [Fe(CN)6]3-, [Fe(CN)6]4-, [Cu(NH3)4]2+ and [Ag(NH3)2]+; van der Waals' forces as a special type of bonding force.
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between types of bonding; deduce bond types from electron configurations; relate the nature of bonding to the properties of compounds.

subtopics.content: Shapes of simple molecules: linear molecules (H2, O2, Cl2, HCl and CO2), non-linear H2O, tetrahedral CH4 and pyramidal NH3.
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between the shapes of simple molecules.

subtopics.content: Radioactivity: types, properties and detection of radiations; natural and artificial radioactivity; nuclear stability and radioactive decay; nuclear reactions including nuclear fusion and fission.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between ordinary chemical and nuclear reactions; differentiate natural and artificial radioactivity; compare properties of nuclear radiations; calculate the half-life of radioactive materials; balance simple nuclear equations; identify applications of radioactivity.

subtopics.content: Unsaturated, saturated and supersaturated solutions; solubility curves and simple deductions; solubility expressed in moles per dm3 and simple calculations.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between types of solutions; interpret solubility curves; calculate the amount of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature; deduce that solubility depends on temperature.

subtopics.content: Solvents for fats, oils, perspiration and paints, and their uses in stain removal.
subtopics.objective: Relate the nature of solvents to their uses.

subtopics.content: True and false solutions, including suspensions and colloids; properties and examples. Harmattan haze and water paints as suspensions; fog, milk, blood, aerosol sprays, emulsion paints and rubber solution as colloids.
subtopics.objective: Differentiate true solutions, suspensions and colloids; compare the properties of true and false solutions; provide typical examples of suspensions and colloids.

subtopics.content: Air: natural gaseous constituents and their proportions, including nitrogen, oxygen, water vapour, carbon(IV) oxide and noble gases such as argon and neon; factors responsible for variations in atmospheric composition; air as a mixture and uses of noble gases.
subtopics.objective: Explain why air exists as a mixture; identify the principle used to separate air components; state reasons for variations in atmospheric composition; specify uses of some constituents of air.

subtopics.content: Air pollution: pollutants such as H2S, CO, SO2, oxides of nitrogen, chlorofluorocarbons and dust; their sources and effects.
subtopics.objective: Identify types of pollution and pollutants; specify pollutant sources; classify pollutants as biodegradable or non-biodegradable; explain environmental effects and identify pollution-control measures.

subtopics.content: Water pollution, including sewage and oil pollution.
subtopics.objective: Identify sources and effects of water pollution and measures for controlling it.

subtopics.content: Soil pollution, including oil spillage and biodegradable and non-biodegradable pollutants.
subtopics.objective: Identify types and sources of soil pollution; classify pollutants; explain their environmental effects and measures for control.

subtopics.content: General characteristics, properties and uses of acids, bases and salts; acid-base indicators; basicity of acids; normal, acidic, basic and double salts. An acid as a substance whose aqueous solution furnishes H3O+ ions or which donates protons. Naturally occurring organic acids including ethanoic, citric and tartaric acids; alums as double salts. Preparation of salts by neutralization, precipitation and reaction of acids with metals; oxides and trioxocarbonate(IV) salts.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish properties of acids and bases; identify types of acids and bases; determine the basicity of acids; differentiate acidity and alkalinity using indicators; identify methods of salt preparation; classify different types of salts.

subtopics.content: Qualitative comparison of conductance in molar solutions of strong and weak acids and bases; relationship between conductance and the amount of ions present.
subtopics.objective: Relate the degree of dissociation to acid and base strength and to conductance.

subtopics.content: pH and pOH scales; simple calculations; significance of pH in everyday life; buffer solutions.
subtopics.objective: Perform simple pH and pOH calculations; explain the significance of pH in everyday life; state applications of buffer solutions.

subtopics.content: Acid-base titrations and titration curves.
subtopics.objective: Identify appropriate acid-base indicators; interpret titration curves; perform simple calculations based on the mole concept.

subtopics.content: Hydrolysis of salts, including NH4Cl, AlCl3, Na2CO3 and CH3COONa.
subtopics.objective: Balance equations for salt hydrolysis; deduce whether the resulting solution is acidic, basic or neutral.

subtopics.content: Oxidation as the addition of oxygen; reduction as the removal of oxygen with the aid of hydrogen; oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer; oxidation numbers; changes in oxidation number and the use of oxidation numbers to balance simple equations.
subtopics.objective: Identify different ways of expressing oxidation and reduction; classify reactions as oxidation or reduction; balance redox equations; deduce oxidation numbers; calculate electron transfer in redox reactions; identify redox species and distinguish oxidizing from reducing agents.

subtopics.content: IUPAC nomenclature of inorganic compounds using oxidation numbers; tests for oxidizing and reducing agents.
subtopics.objective: Apply oxidation numbers when naming inorganic compounds; relate reagents to their oxidizing and reducing abilities.

subtopics.content: Electrolytes and non-electrolytes; Faraday's laws of electrolysis.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish electrolytes from non-electrolytes; perform calculations based on the Faraday as a mole of electrons.

subtopics.content: Electrolysis of dilute H2SO4, aqueous CuSO4, CuCl2 solution, dilute and concentrated NaCl solutions, and fused NaCl; factors affecting the discharge of ions at electrodes.
subtopics.objective: Identify suitable electrodes for different electrolytes; specify electrode reactions; determine electrode products; identify factors affecting electrolysis products.

subtopics.content: Uses of electrolysis, including purification of copper and production of aluminium, sodium, oxygen, chlorine and sodium hydroxide.
subtopics.objective: Specify applications of electrolysis and electrolytic processes.

subtopics.content: Electrochemical cells; electrochemical series: K, Ca, Na, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Sn, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag and Au; half-cell reactions and electrode potentials; simple calculations.
subtopics.objective: State the significance of the electrochemical series; identify electrochemical cells; calculate electrode potentials using half-cell reaction equations.

subtopics.content: Corrosion as an electrolytic process; prevention of iron corrosion by cathodic protection, painting, electroplating and coating with grease or oil.
subtopics.objective: Identify methods of protecting metals against corrosion.

subtopics.content: Energy changes (ΔH) accompanying physical and chemical changes; dissolution of substances in water or reactions with water, including Na, NaOH, K and NH4Cl; endothermic (+ΔH) and exothermic (-ΔH) reactions.
subtopics.objective: Determine the types of heat changes in physical and chemical processes; interpret graphical representations of heat changes.

subtopics.content: Entropy as an order-disorder phenomenon, illustrated by mixing gases and dissolving salts.
subtopics.objective: Relate the physical state of a substance to its degree of orderliness.

subtopics.content: Spontaneity of reactions; ΔG° = 0 as a criterion for equilibrium; ΔG greater than zero for non-spontaneity and ΔG less than zero for spontaneity.
subtopics.objective: Determine the conditions for spontaneity; relate ΔH°, ΔS° and ΔG° as driving forces for chemical reactions; solve simple problems using ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS°.

subtopics.content: Factors affecting reaction rates: temperature, illustrated by reactions between HCl and Na2S2O3 or Mg and HCl; concentration and pressure, illustrated by HCl and Na2S2O3, HCl and marble, and the iodine clock reaction; pressure as a concentration term for gases; surface area, illustrated by powdered and lump marble reacting with HCl; catalysts, illustrated by decomposition of H2O2 or KClO3 in the presence or absence of MnO2.
subtopics.objective: Identify factors affecting reaction rates; determine the effects of temperature; examine the effects of concentration and pressure; describe the effects of surface area; determine suitable catalysts and their effects; identify ways of moderating these effects.

subtopics.content: Reaction-rate curves; activation energy; qualitative treatment of Arrhenius' law and collision theory; effect of light on reactions such as halogenation of alkanes.
subtopics.objective: Interpret reaction-rate curves; solve simple problems on reaction rates; relate reaction rates to the kinetic theory of matter; explain the significance of activation energy; deduce activation energy (Ea) from reaction-rate curves.

subtopics.content: Reversible reactions and factors governing equilibrium position; dynamic equilibrium; Le Chatelier's principle and its industrial applications; equilibrium constant; examples including the action of steam on iron and N2O4 ⇌ 2NO2. No calculations are required for equilibrium constants.
subtopics.objective: Identify factors affecting the equilibrium position of a reaction; predict the effects of each factor on equilibrium position; specify industrial processes where Le Chatelier's principle is applied; determine the effects of factors on the equilibrium constant.

subtopics.content: Hydrogen: commercial production from water gas and cracking of petroleum fractions; laboratory preparation; properties, uses and tests.
subtopics.objective: Predict reagents for laboratory and industrial preparation of hydrogen; identify its properties, uses and specific tests.

subtopics.content: Halogens: chlorine as a representative element; laboratory and industrial preparation by electrolysis; properties and uses, including water sterilization, bleaching and manufacture of HCl, plastics and insecticides. Hydrogen chloride and hydrochloric acid: preparation and properties; chlorides and tests for chlorides.
subtopics.objective: Predict reagents for preparing halogens and their compounds; identify and compare their properties and uses; determine specific tests for gases, compounds and Cl-; predict reagents for the preparation, properties and uses of HCl(g) and HCl(aq).

subtopics.content: Oxygen: laboratory preparation, properties and uses; commercial production from liquid air; acidic, basic, amphoteric and neutral oxides; ozone as an allotrope and its atmospheric importance.
subtopics.objective: Identify oxygen allotropes; explain the environmental significance of ozone; classify oxides and describe their properties.

subtopics.content: Water: formation by combustion of hydrogen; composition by volume; use as a solvent; dissolved atmospheric gases and their biological significance; hard and soft water; temporary and permanent hardness and methods of softening; treatment of water for town supply; water of crystallization, efflorescence, deliquescence and hygroscopy, with examples and uses.
subtopics.objective: Identify uses of water; explain the effects of dissolved atmospheric gases; distinguish hard and soft water; determine causes of hardness and methods of removal; describe town water treatment; distinguish efflorescence, deliquescence, hygroscopy and water of crystallization; identify compounds exhibiting these phenomena.

subtopics.content: Sulphur: uses and allotropes; preparation of allotropes is not required. Preparation, properties and uses of sulphur(IV) oxide; reaction of SO2 with alkalis; trioxosulphate(IV) acid and its salts; action of acids on trioxosulphate(IV) salts; tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, its commercial preparation by the contact process, properties as a dilute acid, oxidizing and dehydrating agent, and uses; tests for SO4^2-, SO3^2- and SO2.
subtopics.objective: Identify sulphur allotropes and their uses; predict reagents for preparing SO2 and H2S and identify their properties and uses; specify the preparation, properties and uses of H2SO4 and H2SO3; determine specific tests for S2-, SO4^2-, H2S, SO2 and SO3^2-.

subtopics.content: Hydrogen sulphide: preparation and properties as a weak acid, reducing agent and precipitating agent; tests for S2- and H2S.
subtopics.objective: Predict reagents for the preparation of H2S; identify its properties and uses; determine specific tests for sulphide ions and hydrogen sulphide.

subtopics.content: Nitrogen: laboratory preparation and production from liquid air. Ammonia: laboratory and industrial preparation by the Haber process; properties and uses; ammonium salts and uses; oxidation of ammonia to nitrogen(IV) oxide and trioxonitrate(V) acid; tests for NH4+, NO2-, and NH3.
subtopics.objective: Specify laboratory and industrial methods of preparing NH3; identify its properties and uses; determine specific tests for NH4+, NH3 and the relevant nitrogen species.

subtopics.content: Trioxonitrate(V) acid: laboratory preparation from ammonia, properties and uses; trioxonitrate(V) salts, action of heat and uses; tests for NO3- and other oxides of nitrogen.
subtopics.objective: Identify reagents for laboratory preparation of HNO3; describe its properties and uses; determine tests for nitrate ions and nitrogen compounds.

subtopics.content: Oxides of nitrogen: properties of N2O, NO and NO2; the nitrogen cycle.
subtopics.objective: Specify properties of N2O, NO and NO2; identify appropriate tests for nitrogen oxides and nitrate ions; examine the relevance of the nitrogen cycle to the environment.

subtopics.content: Carbon: allotropes and their uses and properties; carbon(IV) oxide, laboratory preparation, properties and uses; action of heat on trioxocarbonate(IV) salts; tests for CO3^2-, HCO3- and CO2; carbon(II) oxide, laboratory preparation, properties and effects on blood; sources including charcoal, fires and exhaust fumes; types of coal; products of destructive distillation of wood and coal; coke, gasification, manufacture of synthesis gas and uses.
subtopics.objective: Identify allotropes of carbon; predict reagents for laboratory preparation of CO2 and CO; specify their properties and uses; determine the effects of CO on humans; identify tests for HCO3-, CO3^2- and CO2; identify types of coal and their uses; specify products of destructive distillation of wood and coal; state uses of coke and synthesis gas.

subtopics.content: General properties of metals.
subtopics.objective: Specify the general properties of metals; determine suitable extraction methods; relate extraction methods to metal properties; compare chemical reactivities; specify metal uses; determine specific tests for metallic ions.

subtopics.content: Alkali metals, especially sodium. Sodium hydroxide: production by electrolysis of brine; action on aluminium, zinc and lead ions; uses, including precipitation of metallic hydroxides. Sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) and sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate(IV): production by the Solvay process, properties and uses, including Na2CO3 in glass manufacture. Sodium chloride: occurrence in seawater, uses, economic importance of seawater, recovery of sodium chloride and test for Na+.
subtopics.objective: Describe production of sodium compounds; compare their reactivities; identify their properties and uses; determine specific tests for sodium ions.

subtopics.content: Alkaline-earth metals, especially calcium; calcium oxide, calcium hydroxide and calcium trioxocarbonate(IV), their properties and uses; preparation of calcium oxide from seashells; chemical composition of cement and setting of mortar; test for Ca2+.
subtopics.objective: Describe the preparation, properties and uses of calcium compounds; specify the chemical composition of cement; explain the setting of mortar; identify tests for calcium ions.

subtopics.content: Aluminium: purification of bauxite, electrolytic extraction, properties and uses of aluminium and its compounds; test for Al3+.
subtopics.objective: Describe bauxite purification and aluminium extraction; identify properties and uses of aluminium and its compounds; determine specific tests for aluminium ions.

subtopics.content: Tin: extraction from ores, properties and uses.
subtopics.objective: Specify ores of tin; relate its extraction method to its properties; identify uses of tin.

subtopics.content: Metals of the first transition series: characteristic electron configurations, oxidation states, complex-ion formation, coloured ions and catalysis.
subtopics.objective: Identify general properties of first-row transition metals; explain their characteristic properties; determine IUPAC names of simple transition-metal complexes.

subtopics.content: Iron: extraction from sulphide and oxide ores; properties and uses; different forms of iron, their properties and advantages of steel over iron; tests for Fe2+ and Fe3+.
subtopics.objective: Determine suitable methods for iron extraction; specify properties and uses of iron; identify different forms of iron, their compositions, properties and uses; determine tests for Fe2+ and Fe3+.

subtopics.content: Copper: extraction from sulphide and oxide ores; properties and uses of copper; preparation and uses of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI); test for Cu2+.
subtopics.objective: Identify suitable extraction methods for copper; relate properties of copper and its compounds to their uses; specify the preparation of CuSO4; determine tests for Cu2+.

subtopics.content: Alloys: steel, stainless steel, brass, bronze, type-metal, duralumin, soft solder, permalloy and alnico; constituents and uses.
subtopics.objective: Specify constituents and uses of the listed alloys; compare the properties and uses of alloys with those of pure metals.

subtopics.content: Introduction to tetravalency of carbon; general formulae, IUPAC nomenclature and determination of empirical formulae for the classes of organic compounds in the syllabus.
subtopics.objective: Derive names of organic compounds from their general formulae; relate compound names to structures; relate carbon tetravalency to catenation; classify compounds by functional groups; derive empirical and molecular formulae from data; relate structures and functional groups to properties; derive isomers from a given formula and distinguish types of isomerism.

subtopics.content: Aliphatic hydrocarbons: alkanes, their homologous series and physical properties; substitution reactions and uses of halogenated products; structural isomerism limited to six carbon atoms. Petroleum composition, fractional distillation and major products; cracking, reforming, petrochemicals as starting materials for organic synthesis, petrol quality and octane number.
subtopics.objective: Classify hydrocarbons and distinguish their properties; identify their uses; recognize crude oil as a complex mixture of hydrocarbons; relate petroleum fractions to their properties and uses; relate transformation processes to improved fraction quality.

subtopics.content: Alkenes: structural and geometric isomerism, addition and polymerization reactions; polythene and synthetic rubber as polymerization products; vulcanization and its uses.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish types of isomerism and polymerization; specify the process of vulcanization; identify chemical tests for alkenes.

subtopics.content: Alkynes: ethyne production by the action of water on carbides; simple reactions and properties of ethyne.
subtopics.objective: Specify chemical tests for terminal alkynes; distinguish between aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons.

subtopics.content: Aromatic hydrocarbons, especially benzene: structure, properties and uses.
subtopics.objective: Relate benzene's properties to its structure; distinguish aromatic from aliphatic hydrocarbons.

subtopics.content: Alkanols: primary, secondary and tertiary alkanols; ethanol production by fermentation and from petroleum by-products; local fermentation and distillation examples, including gin from palm wine and other local sources; glycerol as a polyhydric alkanol; reactions of the OH group; oxidation as a distinguishing test among primary, secondary and tertiary alkanols; Lucas test.
subtopics.objective: Compare classes of alkanols; describe processes involved in ethanol production; examine ethanol's importance as an alternative energy source; distinguish the different classes of alkanols.

subtopics.content: Alkanals and alkanones: chemical tests for distinguishing them.
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between alkanals and alkanones.

subtopics.content: Alkanoic acids: chemical reactions including neutralization and esterification; ethanedioic (oxalic) acid as a dicarboxylic acid; benzene carboxylic acid as an aromatic acid.
subtopics.objective: Compare different types of alkanoic acids.

subtopics.content: Alkanoates: formation from alkanoic acids and alkanols; fats and oils as alkanoates; saponification; production of soap and margarine from alkanoates; distinction between detergents and soaps.
subtopics.objective: Identify natural sources of alkanoates; infer products of reactions between alkanoic acids and alkanols; specify methods of producing soap, detergent and margarine; distinguish detergents from soaps.

subtopics.content: Amines (alkanamines): primary, secondary and tertiary classes.
subtopics.objective: Compare the different classes of alkanamines.

subtopics.content: Carbohydrates: classification into mono-, di- and polysaccharides; composition; chemical tests for simple sugars; reaction with concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid; hydrolysis of complex sugars, including cellulose from cotton and starch from cassava; uses of sugar and starch in alcoholic beverages, pharmaceuticals and textiles.
subtopics.objective: Identify natural sources of carbohydrates; compare carbohydrate classes; infer products of hydrolysis and dehydration; determine carbohydrate uses; specify tests for simple sugars.

subtopics.content: Proteins: primary structures, hydrolysis and tests including Ninhydrin, Biuret, Millon's and xanthoproteic tests; enzymes and their functions.
subtopics.objective: Identify the basic structure of proteins; specify methods and products of hydrolysis; identify the various tests for proteins; describe enzyme functions.

subtopics.content: Polymers: natural and synthetic rubber; addition and condensation polymerization; methods of preparation, examples and uses; thermoplastic and thermosetting plastics.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish natural and synthetic polymers; differentiate addition from condensation polymerization; classify natural and commercial polymers and identify their uses; distinguish thermoplastics from thermosetting plastics.

subtopics.content: Chemical industries: types, raw materials and relevance; biotechnology.
subtopics.objective: Classify chemical industries by products; identify raw materials used by each industry; distinguish fine chemicals from heavy chemicals; state the relevance of these industries; relate industrial processes to biotechnology.

subtopics.content: The solar system, planets and satellite; composition of the Earth, including the atmosphere, lithosphere and hydrosphere.
subtopics.objective: State the composition of the solar system; list the planets; identify the segments of the Earth; name Earth's natural satellite; identify the smallest planet, which is also the farthest from the Sun.
